name: 3D Pinball: Space Cadet
epitaph: Tilt. Tilt. Tilt. Game over, Cadet.
cause_of_death: Windows XP was its last home; it was left out of Windows Vista.
note: died = Vista RTM (Nov 2006); tribute is Star Cadet (MIT), an original-asset remake
game_credit: Star Cadet by the Star Cadet authors (MIT). Original-art remake; no Microsoft code or art.

name: 3D Pipes
epitaph: Here lies the plumber's nightmare, still connecting.
cause_of_death: The OpenGL screensaver from Windows NT 3.5 was dropped after Windows XP.
note: born = Windows NT 3.5 (1994); last in Windows XP

name: Road Rash
epitaph: Kicked off the bike, but never off our hearts.
cause_of_death: The series stalled after its last new game, Jailbreak, in 2000.
note: died = last new game (Jailbreak, PS1 2000); a GBA port followed in 2003
game_credit: A tribute written by Meta Muse Spark for Raise Dead (AI-generated, original art).

name: Google Reader
cause_of_death: Google closed it, citing falling use, and told readers to export.

name: Clicky the Paperclip
epitaph: It looks like you're writing a eulogy.
cause_of_death: Switched off by default in 2001, then removed from the office suite for good in 2007.
note: born = Office 97 debut

name: Winamp
epitaph: It really whipped. Then it rested.
cause_of_death: AOL announced the end of downloads and support in late 2013.
note: Brand later sold and revived; 2013 = AOL's shutdown announcement (Dec 20, 2013)
game_credit: A tribute written by Meta Muse Spark for Raise Dead (AI-generated, original art).

name: Unmarked Grave
epitaph: Name the lost one, and it shall rise.
cause_of_death: Nobody remembers. Perhaps you do.
note: placeholder grave for user-summoned apps

name: Orkut
cause_of_death: Google retired it once its users moved on, mostly to Facebook.
note: huge in India and Brazil

name: MSN Messenger
cause_of_death: Microsoft retired it in 2013 and moved users to Skype.
note: China service ran until 2014

name: Internet Explorer
cause_of_death: Microsoft ended support in favour of its newer Edge browser.
note: still supported on some LTSC editions

name: Adobe Flash Player
epitaph: Plugin required to view this afterlife.
cause_of_death: Adobe set an end-of-life date as browsers moved to open web standards.
note: born = renamed Macromedia Flash Player in 1996 (FutureSplash earlier)

name: Vine
epitaph: Six seconds was all it needed.
cause_of_death: Twitter shut the app down as creators drifted to other platforms.

name: Google+
epitaph: In many circles, mourned by few.
cause_of_death: Google shut the consumer version after low engagement and a data bug.

name: Yahoo! Messenger
cause_of_death: Yahoo pulled the plug after a short-lived rebuild failed to catch on.
note: born = launch as Yahoo! Pager

name: Myspace (classic)
epitaph: Tom is still your friend. Always.
cause_of_death: A 2013 redesign replaced the old site and wiped users' blogs.
note: Myspace still exists; 'classic' died with the June 2013 redesign

name: Friendster
epitaph: The friend who got there first.
cause_of_death: It suspended services after users left for newer networks.
note: Wikipedia notes a relaunch in April 2026

name: Stadia
cause_of_death: Google closed the cloud gaming service after it failed to win players.

name: Picasa
cause_of_death: Google folded it into Google Photos.
note: born = original Lifescape release; Google bought it in 2004

name: iPod classic
cause_of_death: Apple discontinued it as phones took over music.
note: born = original iPod 2001; 'classic' name from 2007

name: AOL Instant Messenger
cause_of_death: AOL discontinued it as chatting moved to phones and social apps.

name: ICQ
cause_of_death: Its final owner shut the service down in 2024.

name: Skype
cause_of_death: Microsoft retired it in favour of Teams.

name: GeoCities
cause_of_death: Yahoo closed the free hosting service in 2009.

name: Napster (original)
cause_of_death: Copyright lawsuits forced the original file-sharing service offline.
note: brand later relaunched as a paid service

name: LimeWire
cause_of_death: A US court injunction ordered it shut down in 2010.

name: Flappy Bird
cause_of_death: Its creator pulled it from app stores, saying it was too addictive.

name: Club Penguin
cause_of_death: Disney closed its servers to make way for a mobile successor.

name: FarmVille
cause_of_death: It closed when Facebook stopped supporting Flash games.

name: BlackBerry Messenger
cause_of_death: The consumer service shut down after users moved to other chat apps.
note: born year not confirmed on Wikipedia intro (uncertain)

name: Hike Messenger
cause_of_death: Hike closed messaging after failing to compete with global giants.
note: popular in India; launch given as Dec 11 or 12, 2012

name: Windows Phone
cause_of_death: Microsoft stopped development as apps and users went to Android and iOS.
note: died = Windows 10 Mobile end of life

name: Zune
cause_of_death: Microsoft replaced it with Xbox Music and Video.
note: hardware ended Oct 2011

name: Google Wave
cause_of_death: Google ended it after few people understood what to use it for.

name: Google Glass (Explorer)
epitaph: Saw the future a bit too soon.
cause_of_death: Google halted the consumer edition amid privacy worries and weak demand.
note: Enterprise Edition lasted to 2023

name: Netscape Navigator
epitaph: It showed us the way, then lost it.
cause_of_death: AOL ended development and support after its share collapsed.

name: AltaVista
cause_of_death: Yahoo redirected it to Yahoo Search in 2013.

name: Encarta
cause_of_death: Microsoft discontinued it as free online encyclopedias took over.

name: Windows Movie Maker
cause_of_death: Microsoft discontinued it in favour of newer video editors.

name: Kinect
epitaph: It saw us dance. It kept quiet.
cause_of_death: Microsoft ended production after game support dried up.
note: died = end of Xbox One Kinect production

name: Google Hangouts
cause_of_death: Google moved its users over to Google Chat.

name: iGoogle
cause_of_death: Google retired it, saying users no longer needed a portal page.

name: Pebble
cause_of_death: The company went insolvent and sold its assets to Fitbit.
note: online services ended June 2018
